product: KONGSBERG supplies JSM strike missiles, NASAMS air defence, PROTECTOR remote weapon systems and counter-drone systems, Kongsberg Maritime ship automation and propulsion, HUGIN autonomous underwater vehicles and Aegir sonars, and N3X maritime surveillance satellites.
demand: Demand is record-high: Q2 2026 order intake of NOK 17,067m and backlog of NOK 157,540m, driven by NATO rearmament, counter-drone orders to Poland worth NOK 16bn, and JSM orders from Germany worth NOK 3.5bn and from the US Air Force.
pricing_power: Not evidenced in sources read. Management credits higher volumes and strong project execution, not price, for improved profitability, and no pricing commentary was found on the investor relations site or in the press releases read.
competition: Not quantified in the sources read. Evidence is selection outcomes only: Belgium selected NASAMS, Canada became the sixth JSM nation, Kongsberg won a follow-on PROTECTOR contract for Canada ACSV, and it is a key partner on the 212CD submarine combat system.
team: CEO Eirik Harald Lie; Kongsberg Maritime CEO Lisa Edvardsen Haugan; Discovery President Camilla Kiss; Defence Systems President Kjetil Reiten Myhra; Missiles and Aerostructures head Oyvind Kolset. The Norwegian state holds 50.004pc of the shares.
market_strategy: Grow with NATO and allied defence budgets, expand in the United States and Canada via acquisitions (Zone 5 Technologies, Sonatech) and partnerships (MDA Space, Telesat), and scale manufacturing including metal additive manufacturing, targeting NOK 100bn revenue by 2029.
bull: Q2 2026 (13 Jul): revenue NOK 10,389m up 31pc, EBIT NOK 1,669m, order intake NOK 17,067m, backlog NOK 157,540m; NATO rearmament demand with named orders (Poland NOK 16bn, Germany JSM NOK 3.5bn).
bear: Q2 EBIT margin missed BofA expectations (15 Jul 2026); Maritime EBITDA margin 12.5pc with FX drag; Morgan Stanley downgraded to underweight 7 Jul 2026; shares below 10 Apr high of 352.8 NOK.
falsifier: Q3 2026 report on 29 Oct 2026 showing EBIT margin below 16pc or order intake below NOK 17,067m would break the growth-and-margin bull case.
web_what_changed: Q2 2026 (13 Jul 2026): revenue NOK 10,389m up 31pc, EBIT NOK 1,669m, margin 16.1pc, order intake NOK 17,067m, backlog NOK 157,540m. Other 90-day items: USAF JSM order about USD 100m (16 Jul), CAMP XLUUV selection (15 Jul), Sonatech acquisition closed (1 Sep), Canada PROTECTOR NOK 1.1bn (20 Aug), N3X satellites (24 Aug), MDA/Telesat agreements (22 Sep), NTNU HUGIN (24 Sep).
web_not_known_yesterday: Nothing dated 25 Sep 2026 found; latest primary item is the NTNU HUGIN 6000 purchase announced 24 Sep 2026 at the Trondheim Defence Conference. Same-day quotes differ between aggregators: 315.0 NOK on TradingView versus 313.20 NOK on stockanalysis.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Demand-led and volume-led. The company attributes improved profit to higher volumes and strong project execution with record order intake, while Kongsberg Maritime cites newbuild volume. No price or unit-price disclosure was found, so price contribution is unevidenced; mix is shifting toward defence (JSM, NASAMS, counter-drone).
web_suppliers: Named suppliers and partners: EOS and AMCM (metal additive manufacturing), Kongsberg NanoAvionics (satellite platforms), KSAT (ground segment), Telesat Lightspeed (LEO connectivity), MDA Space, Fugro (SEAWATCH buoy), Raytheon, Diehl Defence, MBDA, Helsing, Oceaneering. No supplier constraint was disclosed; only FX and slower aftermarket decisions were cited as pressures.
web_customers: State and NATO buyers dominate: Norwegian Armed Forces, US Air Force, US Navy, Germany, Canada, Poland, Kuwait, Japan, Australia, with General Dynamics Land Systems-Canada as an industrial customer. Concentration is high because customers are governments; the Norwegian state owns 50.004pc of the company itself.
web_who_loses: Inference from selection outcomes, not a company statement: rival vendors that lost the same competitions Kongsberg won, such as competing air-defence, counter-drone, remote-weapon and strike-missile suppliers in the Poland C-UAS, Belgium NASAMS, Canada ACSV and JSM, and 212CD submarine programmes.
web_contradicting_evidence: Q2 EBIT margin missed Bank of America expectations (15 Jul 2026). Kongsberg Maritime EBITDA margin was 12.5pc with FX pressure and slower large aftermarket upgrades (13 Jul 2026). Morgan Stanley downgraded to underweight on 7 Jul 2026. Shares fell on results day and are down 2.44pc on the week, below the 10 Apr 2026 high of 352.8 NOK.
web_if_management_right: The NOK 157,540m backlog converts into revenue, supporting the stated ambition of NOK 100bn revenue by 2029 and NOK 150bn by 2033 with EBIT margin above 16pc; consensus FY2026 revenue is about NOK 43.2bn, 37pc growth, with EPS about 7.41.
web_if_management_wrong: Margins and execution break first: Kongsberg Maritime at 12.5pc EBITDA margin, FX drag, slower aftermarket decisions and long delivery schedules (USAF JSM deliveries run to June 2030) mean backlog converts slowly, and any delivery slippage or cost overrun hits EBIT before it hits revenue.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Named partners and suppliers: EOS and AMCM, MDA Space, Telesat, Oceaneering, Kongsberg NanoAvionics, KSAT, Diehl Defence, MBDA, Helsing, Fugro, General Dynamics Land Systems-Canada, Raytheon on NASAMS, plus Norwegian shipyards and the newbuild supply chain behind Kongsberg Maritime record backlog.
